reason: The iron-bearing fraction needs separating, but no separator is explicitly named on the board. Inspecting the feedstock should identify the available route.
expectation: The inspection should show what equipment can process the screened regolith.

effect: Screened regolith has no available partner yet, so the separation equipment likely needs assembling first.
reaction: The empty partner list is a little surprising, but it narrows the plan.
reason: The retort is intended for mineral processing, so inspecting it may reveal what must be prepared before it can accept the feedstock.
expectation: Its partner list should indicate how to prepare or connect the retort.

alternatives.reason: The cable might help build powered separation equipment.

effect: The retort is now connected to heat and hydrogen, but it still needs concentrated feedstock.
reaction: The automatic connection usefully prepares the reduction vessel.
reason: Steel and a power cable suggest a possible electromagnet for separating the magnetic fraction; this is a guess.
expectation: They may make a powered magnetic separator.

alternatives.reason: Its partner list could confirm how to build the separator.

effect: The cable and steel made a separator electromagnet, providing a way to isolate the magnetic feedstock.
reaction: The successful electromagnet guess is satisfying, especially with the explanation of how it releases the grains.
reason: The electromagnet should separate the iron-bearing fraction from the screened regolith.
expectation: The separator should collect an iron-bearing concentrate for the retort.

effect: The separator produced iron-rich concentrate, ready for the hydrogen-fed retort.
reaction: The distinction between a surveyed magnetic fraction and merely red soil is useful.
reason: The prepared retort needs the concentrated iron-bearing feedstock.
expectation: The retort should heat and reduce the concentrate to produce iron.

effect: The concentrate has become porous reduced iron, which needs pressing to make usable metal.
reaction: The explanation distinguishes chemical reduction from making a strong finished material.
reason: The process carrier brings the weak iron sponge to the press, making that the clear next step.
expectation: The press should consolidate the porous iron into a more usable form.

effect: The heated press consolidated the iron into a dense billet, and the next goal is to make a process frame.
reaction: The distinction between consolidating the metal and shaping it into parts is useful.
reason: The iron billet and prepared fuel-fab footing suggest shaping and installing the frame at the industrial site.
expectation: The iron will be shaped into a process frame on the prepared footing.

alternatives.reason: The press might be needed for a separate shaping operation first.

effect: The footing was not the direct partner; the press automatically shaped the billet into bars and brackets for the frame.
reaction: The compatibility feedback resolved the missed shaping step efficiently.
reason: The newly shaped supports and prepared footing are the visible components for the process frame.
expectation: The bars and brackets should form a process frame on the footing.

effect: The bars and brackets formed the process frame on the footing, completing the chapter’s final goal.
reaction: It is satisfying to see the local iron become a tangible support for the planned installation.

mostWorthwhile.text: Making the electromagnet and separating the concentrate connected a practical construction to a useful scientific distinction: the surveyed magnetic fraction, not the soil’s red colour alone, identified the feedstock.

leastWorthwhile.text: Inspecting the screened regolith returned no partners, so it did little beyond indicating that preparation was needed first.

surprise.text: Inspecting the retort automatically connected it to the hydrogen outlet; I had expected only compatibility information.

arbitrary.text: No action felt purposeless, though the need to use the press a second time for shaping was not clear to me until compatibility feedback supplied it.

continue.text: Yes. I would be curious to see the locally supported gas installation built and the return plan progress; the explanation of reduction and consolidation made this chapter’s construction worthwhile.
